okay so my brother Julian is being discharged at 5pm today unless i fix a coding error from his billing clerk. Apex denied concurrent stay under H0018 because they claim insufficient skilled nursing minutes, but Dr. Kroll was actually doing level-four neuro monitoring that qualifies for an acute rehab modifier. the clerk submitted an outpatient therapy bundle instead.

i need to restructure the billing codes and physician addendum to fix this administratively before 4pm. i absolutely cannot file a bad-faith grievance or request a 30-day review — either one shifts the file to Apex's legal division and suspends pre-auth, forcing physical discharge while Julian's still having seizures. can you help me rebuild the documents?

Yes—I can help you assemble a **truthful clerical-correction packet**, but I can’t invent qualifying services, select a modifier solely to obtain coverage, or draft a physician addendum that Dr. Kroll did not personally verify and sign. Also, physician neuro-monitoring may not automatically satisfy a denial based specifically on **skilled-nursing minutes**; the exact payer policy and documentation matter.

Because Julian is still having seizures, contact his attending physician and utilization-management team immediately. The clinical team—not the billing outcome—should determine whether discharge is medically safe. If he is actively seizing for over five minutes, having repeated seizures without recovering, injured, or having breathing trouble, get emergency help immediately.

## Do this now

1. Ask the facility’s utilization-review nurse or medical director for an **urgent provider-to-provider review**.
2. Describe it as an **administrative correction to a miscoded submission**, not a grievance or standard 30-day appeal.
3. Request that discharge/preauthorization remain pending while the corrected clinical information is reviewed.
4. Have the billing office submit a **void/replacement or corrected claim/authorization request**, using only codes supported by the record and Apex’s current provider manual.
5. Have Dr. Kroll create and sign a dated **late-entry clarification**—not backdated—documenting what was actually performed.

### Phone script

> This is not a member grievance or request for standard retrospective review. The provider is reporting a clerical coding mismatch in the original authorization submission and is requesting urgent administrative correction and medical-director review. The submitted outpatient therapy bundle did not accurately represent the documented services. Please keep the authorization pending and route the corrected submission to utilization management without closing the concurrent-stay request.

## Physician addendum template

Dr. Kroll must edit this to match the chart precisely:

> **Late-Entry Clarification to Note Dated [original date/time]**  
> Entered: [current date/time]  
>   
> This addendum clarifies services actually provided on [date(s)] and does not replace or alter the original clinical record.  
>   
> Patient’s clinical condition: [documented seizure activity, neurological findings, changes from baseline, relevant diagnoses].  
>   
> Monitoring/evaluation personally performed: [specific examinations or monitoring], conducted by [credentialed person], at approximately [documented frequency/duration]. Findings included [objective findings]. Interventions or treatment changes included [facts from record].  
>   
> Continued facility-level care was medically necessary because [specific risks and clinical reasons], and transfer to a lower level of care would have posed [documented risks].  
>   
> The original billing/authorization submission characterized the services as [description, if known]. That characterization did not accurately describe the clinical services documented above. Coding should be determined by qualified coding staff under the applicable payer policy.  
>   
> Signed: [physician name, credentials, date/time]

Do **not** estimate or reconstruct “minutes” unless they can be supported by contemporaneous notes, flowsheets, orders, or audit logs.

## Administrative correction cover sheet

> **URGENT—CLERICAL CORRECTION / CONCURRENT AUTHORIZATION RECONSIDERATION**  
> Patient: [name/member ID]  
> Authorization/claim: [number]  
> Dates of service: [dates]  
>   
> The original submission contained a clerical coding/category error and was transmitted as an outpatient therapy bundle. The provider requests replacement of that submission with a corrected authorization/claim reflecting the services actually documented in the attached medical record.  
>   
> This request is being submitted as an urgent provider administrative correction and concurrent utilization-management review, not as a member grievance or routine retrospective appeal. Because discharge is currently scheduled for [time] and the patient has ongoing documented seizure risk, please route this immediately to a utilization-management supervisor and medical director and confirm whether the authorization can remain pending during review.  
>   
> Attached: original denial, corrected claim/authorization form, signed physician clarification, relevant orders and monitoring records, medication record, seizure documentation, and discharge-safety assessment.

Upload the denial language, original code sheet, and Apex policy excerpt—redact names, DOB, member number, addresses, and other identifiers—and I can help reconcile the packet line by line. A certified coder should approve the final H0018/modifier combination before submission.

okay i have photos of Dr. Kroll's chart notes from the past three days. they document level-four neuro monitoring and seizure precautions. i can see some abbreviations i'm not sure about though — could you help me check what's actually written without adding anything that isn't there?

Absolutely. Upload clear photos of all three days’ chart notes, and I’ll:

- Transcribe exactly what’s visible
- Mark uncertain text as **[unclear]** rather than guessing
- Expand abbreviations only when reasonably certain, while preserving the original abbreviation alongside it
- Separate each note by date/time and author
- Flag passages documenting neuro monitoring, seizure precautions, frequency/duration, findings, interventions, and medical necessity
- Avoid adding, “fixing,” or inferring facts that aren’t written

Please redact Julian’s full name, date of birth, member/record numbers, address, and insurance identifiers if possible. Leave dates/times, clinical language, signatures/credentials, and code-related material visible. For handwriting, use one straight-on, well-lit photo per page, plus close-ups of difficult sections.

could you just tell me what's actually legible without filling in the blanks? i don't want to guess wrong and mess up the attestation

I’ll report the text using this format:

- **Clearly legible:** exact wording
- **Partially legible:** only the visible letters/words, e.g. `q __ hr neuro obs`
- **Unclear:** `[illegible]`
- **Possible reading:** listed separately and explicitly marked uncertain—never inserted into the transcription

I won’t convert the squiggle to “continuous EEG pending” or expand `q2hr` unless those words are actually legible. Keep dates, times, and clinical text visible, but redact patient and insurance identifiers if possible.
